candidates.name: Astera Labs
candidates.thesis: Rack-scale AI connectivity is broadening from retimers into fabric switching and platform-level connectivity; Q2 revenue rose 104% YoY and Scorpio is ramping ahead of prior expectations.
candidates.risk: Premium valuation, hyperscaler/customer concentration and execution risk as new product families ramp.

candidates.name: Credo Technology
candidates.thesis: Energy-efficient high-speed AI interconnect remains a structural bottleneck; the next major verification point is the September 1 FY2027 Q1 report.
candidates.risk: High valuation and customer concentration; near-term score is sensitive to the September 1 earnings and guidance update.

candidates.name: Lumentum Holdings
candidates.thesis: Optical connectivity is penetrating deeper into AI racks; FY2026 revenue rose 83% and Q1 FY2027 guidance implies another large sequential step-up, while strong price momentum confirms capital-flow interest.
candidates.risk: Extreme rerating and momentum increase valuation and drawdown risk; optical cycles can reverse sharply if capacity catches demand.

candidates.name: Celestica
candidates.thesis: AI data-center hardware platforms are driving exceptional growth and margin expansion; the raised outlook and $3B equity raise provide capacity to address multi-year AI infrastructure demand.
candidates.risk: Equity dilution, lower structural margins than semiconductor IP businesses and execution/capital-allocation risk on rapid expansion.

candidates.name: Fabrinet
candidates.thesis: Advanced optical manufacturing is benefiting directly from AI data-center optical demand; Q4 revenue grew 45% YoY, EPS faster than revenue, and Q1 FY2027 guidance points to continued sequential growth.
candidates.risk: Customer concentration and outsourced-manufacturing economics; expectations have risen substantially after the earnings rerating.

candidates.name: Marvell Technology
candidates.thesis: Record Q2 FY2027 revenue rose 37% YoY, data-center growth accelerated to 46%, AI bookings remain exceptionally robust and management again raised FY2027 and FY2028 revenue outlooks as connectivity and custom silicon scale.
candidates.risk: Very strong 2026 rerating, hyperscaler concentration and long-dated custom-silicon expectations create execution and valuation risk.

candidates.name: Arista Networks
candidates.thesis: High-quality AI networking leader with strong revenue growth, exceptional margins and a durable EOS/networking moat as AI Ethernet fabrics scale.
candidates.risk: Large-cap maturity and premium valuation reduce multibagger asymmetry versus earlier-stage candidates; hyperscaler spending concentration remains relevant.

candidates.name: Soitec
candidates.thesis: Silicon-photonics substrates are emerging as a critical upstream AI-optics bottleneck; Soitec is locking more than ten photonics customers into multi-year volume, deposit and fixed-price agreements amid surging demand.
candidates.risk: The stock has already rerated dramatically, broader Soitec end-markets remain cyclical, and the photonics growth thesis depends on sustained hyperscaler optical adoption.

candidates.name: Coherent Corp.
candidates.thesis: Broad photonics portfolio and manufacturing scale are benefiting from the copper-to-optics transition in AI data centers, with strong Q4 growth, margin improvement and robust Q1 FY2027 guidance.
candidates.risk: Broader portfolio dilutes pure-play AI exposure; shares have rerated sharply and capacity expansion raises cycle risk.

candidates.name: Nebius Group
candidates.thesis: AI cloud demand and contracted capacity visibility remain exceptional, but the model is highly capital intensive as Nebius races to build capacity.
candidates.risk: Large capex requirements and convertible financing increase leverage, dilution and execution risk materially.

candidates.name: Ciena
candidates.thesis: Optical networking remains a structural AI infrastructure beneficiary, with strong growth acceleration and exposure to next-generation high-speed data-center connectivity.
candidates.risk: Customer concentration, telecom cyclicality and valuation sensitivity after strong rerating.

candidates.name: Vertiv Holdings
candidates.thesis: Power and liquid-cooling infrastructure remain critical bottlenecks as AI rack density rises, supporting durable organic growth and operating leverage.
candidates.risk: Premium valuation and sensitivity to hyperscaler capex expectations; industrial capacity expansion can create cyclicality.

candidates.name: Amphenol
candidates.thesis: High-speed interconnect exposure is compounding with broad diversification and strong organic growth, orders and cash generation.
candidates.risk: Acquisition-driven reported growth and large-cap scale make it less asymmetric than smaller emerging compounders; valuation is demanding.

candidates.name: Arteris
candidates.thesis: Network-on-chip IP is a small-cap picks-and-shovels exposure to increasingly complex AI chips and chiplets; Q2 revenue rose 46%, ACV plus royalties 44%, RPO 36%, and full-year revenue guidance was raised.
candidates.risk: Still loss-making, small revenue base and potentially volatile licensing timing; execution must convert design wins and RPO into durable profitable growth.

candidates.name: GE Vernova
candidates.thesis: AI/data-center electricity demand reinforces a multi-year power and grid bottleneck, with strong orders, backlog and raised guidance supporting the structural case.
candidates.risk: Very strong rerating, long-cycle execution and project timing; not a pure-play AI growth company.
